cards.text: Out on the Mount of Olives, a crowd came for Jesus (Luke 22:39, 47). Now they seize Him and take Him into the house of the high priest. Peter, one of Jesus' twelve disciples (Luke 6:13-14), is coming too.

cards.question: Jesus is being led into the high priest's house. How does Peter follow Him?

cards.text: People kindle a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sit down together, and Peter sits right down among them. Like walking into the wrong meeting at work and just sitting down and NODDING like you belong.
Then a servant girl sees Peter in the firelight and looks at him intently. Not a glance, friend. A LOOK.

cards.question: The servant girl studying Peter in the firelight speaks up. What does she say about him?

answers.text: He works for the high priest

cards.question: When the servant girl says Peter was with Jesus, Peter tells her he knows Jesus.

cards.text: “Woman, I do not know Him,” Peter says. That's the face you make when your phone goes off in a quiet room and you look around at everybody like, “Wow. Whose phone is THAT?”

cards.question: A short time later, someone else tells Peter, “You also are one of them.” Peter denies it again.

cards.text: Peter says, “Man, I am not.” About an hour later, another man insists Peter was with Jesus, and this one has a reason.

cards.question: A man in the high priest's courtyard insists Peter was with Jesus. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Peter came in with the crowd

cards.text: Some things you just can't hide, friend, and a stamper with a mustache THIS big would know. “Man, I do not know what you are talking about,” Peter replies anyway.

cards.question: Peter's third denial is still coming out of his mouth. What happens before he even finishes?

cards.text: That rooster did NOT wait for Peter to finish his sentence, friend. Then someone turns and looks right at Peter.

cards.question: After the rooster crows, Jesus turns and looks at Peter.

cards.text: And in that moment, Peter remembers something the Lord had told him earlier. Something about a rooster.

cards.question: Peter remembers what the Lord told him: before the rooster crows today, Peter will deny Him ___ times.
Peter has just remembered the Lord's words about the rooster. He goes outside, and he ___ bitterly.

cards.text: Now back to Jesus. The men holding Him start in on Him, and friend, this part is hard to read. Stay with me.

cards.question: The men holding Jesus began to ___ Him and ___ Him.

cards.text: Then they blindfold Him. And they keep demanding something.

cards.question: The men holding Jesus have blindfolded Him. What do they keep demanding?

answers.text: That He prophesy who hit Him
That He bow to the high priest
That He call His disciples back

cards.text: And they say many other blasphemous things against Him. Then the council of the elders of the people meets together.

cards.question: The council of the elders meets at daybreak.
The council of the elders of the people meets together. Who is in it?

cards.text: They lead Jesus into their Sanhedrin and say, “If You are the Christ, tell us.” No small talk. Straight to it.

cards.question: Jesus tells the council that if He tells them, they will believe Him.

cards.text: Jesus answers, “If I tell you, you will not believe. And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.” But He's not finished.

cards.question: Jesus keeps going in front of the council. From now on, where does He say the Son of Man will be seated?

answers.text: At the right hand of the power of God
In the holy temple of the living God
On the holy mountain of the house of God

cards.question: Jesus has said the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God. What do they all ask Him next?

answers.text: If He is the Son of God
If He is the king of Israel
If He is a prophet from Galilee

cards.text: Jesus replies, “You say that I am.” Now watch the council.

cards.question: After Jesus says “You say that I am,” the council says they still need more testimony.

cards.text: “We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips,” they declare. Keep your apron on, friend. This story keeps going.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match what Peter does. Walking into the wrong meeting is an accident. Peter followed Jesus on purpose (Luke 22:54) and chose to sit down among the people at the fire (Luke 22:55). The joke also hints at a reason for sitting there (pretending to belong) that the text never gives.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "Then a servant girl sees Peter in the firelight and looks at him intently." / "Not a glance, friend." / "A LOOK."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "Now back to Jesus." / "The men holding Him start in on Him, and friend, this part is hard to read." / "Stay with me."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Both right answers are verbs from the same line, and each is tied to a fixed blank (mock in blank 1, beat in blank 2). A baker who correctly picks "beat" then "mock" would be marked wrong. Only the verse's word order separates the two, so the card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "They lead Jesus into their Sanhedrin and say, 'If You are the Christ, tell us.'" / "No small talk." / "Straight to it."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the two sentences Papa Dorin quotes from Jesus (Luke 22:67-68), plus "But He's not finished."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card sets up being seated, a throne or a right hand. Card 10 only says "But He's not finished." The baker is left to guess the wording of Jesus' line from three similar, Bible-sounding phrases. That makes the card luck, not an informed guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to supply the exact phrase that finishes Jesus' sentence in Luke 22:69. That is guessing the next words of a line, not reasoning about what happens or what it means.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
